label: Fishes, gilled animals and serpents have no testicles
claim: No fish, no other gill-bearing animal and no serpent has testicles; nor does any footless animal except those that are viviparous within themselves.
quote: No fish is furnished with testicles, nor any other creature that has gills, nor any serpent whatever: nor, in short, any animal devoid of feet, save such only as are viviparous within themselves.
scope: fishes, gill-bearing animals, serpents (snakes), footless animals other than the internally viviparous (cetaceans)
measurable_quantities: presence or absence of testes in male fishes and snakes
candidate_data: Comparative reproductive anatomy annotated in Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase; Animal Diversity Web species accounts.

label: Birds, oviparous quadrupeds and the hedgehog have internal testicles near the loin
claim: Birds have testicles placed internally close to the loin, as do oviparous quadrupeds such as the lizard, the tortoise and the crocodile, and among viviparous animals the hedgehog.
quote: Birds are furnished with testicles, but these are internally situated, close to the loin. The case is similar with oviparous quadrupeds, such as the lizard, the tortoise and the crocodile; and among the viviparous animals this peculiarity is found in the hedgehog.
scope: birds; oviparous quadrupeds (lizards, turtles, crocodilians); hedgehog
measurable_quantities: position of the testes (internal, near kidneys) in birds, reptiles and hedgehogs
candidate_data: Comparative anatomy in Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase; literature on testicular descent across mammals; Animal Diversity Web.

label: Bird testicles enlarge greatly in the breeding season
claim: Before the breeding season the testicles of birds are small or invisible, but during the breeding season they become greatly enlarged in all birds.
quote: before the breeding season the organ is small in some birds and quite invisible in others, but during the season the organ in all cases is greatly enlarged.
scope: birds, notably the ring-dove and the partridge
measurable_quantities: testis mass or volume in and out of the breeding season
candidate_data: Published measurements of seasonal gonadal recrudescence in birds; avian reproductive physiology literature.

label: Selachians are internally oviparous and externally viviparous
claim: The dogfish and the other selachians (footless gilled animals that bear live young) produce eggs inside the body, and the eggs turn into young within the womb before birth.
quote: With animals devoid of feet that are internally oviparous and viviparous externally, as is the case with the dogfish and the other so-called Selachians
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode (oviparity, aplacental or placental viviparity) per species
candidate_data: Reproductive mode fields in FishBase; chondrichthyan life-history compilations.

label: The viper is the only viviparous serpent
claim: Serpents as a rule lay eggs; the viper is the only serpent that bears live young, and it does so by first producing eggs internally.
quote: Serpents as a rule are oviparous, the viper being the only viviparous member of the genus. The viper is, previously to external parturition, oviparous internally
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode (oviparous or viviparous) across snake species
candidate_data: The Reptile Database species accounts and published squamate reproductive-mode compilations.

label: Horned animals, hare, mouse and bat have cotyledons in the pregnant womb
claim: Pregnant females of horned animals lacking upper front teeth have cotyledons in the womb, as do the hare, the mouse and the bat; all other viviparous footed animals with teeth in both jaws have a smooth womb with the embryo attached directly to it.
quote: the females of horned nonambidental animals are furnished with cotyledons in the womb when they are pregnant, and such is the case, among ambidentals, with the hare, the mouse, and the bat
scope: horned ruminants (non-ambidentals, lacking upper incisors); hare, mouse, bat; other viviparous quadrupeds
measurable_quantities: placental type (cotyledonary, discoid, diffuse, zonary) per species
candidate_data: Comparative placentation data compiled in the literature (e.g. Mossman's survey) and in Phenoscape anatomy annotations.

label: The great blood-vessels originate in the heart, not the head
claim: The two great blood-vessels (the great vein and the aorta) have their origin in the heart, not, as earlier writers held, in the head or brain.
quote: These blood-vessels have their origins in the heart, for they traverse the other viscera, in whatever direction they happen to run, without in any way losing their distinctive characteristic as blood-vessels
measurable_quantities: anatomical origin of the vena cava and aorta
candidate_data: Vertebrate cardiovascular anatomy in Uberon and standard anatomical atlases.

label: The heart has three chambers, all visible only in the largest animals
claim: The heart has three chambers; in small animals even the largest chamber is scarcely visible, in medium-sized animals the second is scarcely visible, and only in the largest animals are all three distinctly seen.
quote: In the case of the smaller animals even the largest of the chambers is scarcely discernible; the second larger is scarcely discernible in animals of medium size; but in the largest animals all three chambers are distinctly seen.
measurable_quantities: number of heart chambers across vertebrate taxa
relation of chamber visibility to body size
candidate_data: Comparative cardiac anatomy in Uberon and Phenoscape; body mass from AnAge or PanTHERIA.

label: The brain contains no blood and no vein
claim: In all animals the brain itself is bloodless, and no vein, large or small, runs within it; veins end in the membrane around the brain.
quote: The brain itself in all animals is destitute of blood, and no vein, great or small, holds its course therein.
measurable_quantities: presence of blood vessels within brain tissue
candidate_data: Neurovascular anatomy in standard anatomical atlases and Uberon.

label: Fibres in the blood cause it to coagulate
claim: Blood coagulates because of a fibrous matter it contains; if the fibre is left in, the blood coagulates, and if it is removed, the blood cannot coagulate.
quote: If this fibre be left in the blood, the blood will coagulate; if it be removed or extracted, the blood is found to be incapable of coagulation.
measurable_quantities: clotting of whole blood versus defibrinated blood
candidate_data: Standard haematology on defibrination and clotting; comparative coagulation studies.

label: Deer, roe and antelope blood lacks fibre and clots weakly
claim: The blood of the deer, the roe, the antelope and some other animals lacks the coagulating fibre, and so does not coagulate as firmly as the blood of other animals.
quote: we fail to find it in the blood of the deer, the roe, the antelope, and some other animals; and, owing to this deficiency of the fibrous tissue, the blood of these animals does not coagulate to the extent observed in the blood of other animals.
measurable_quantities: plasma fibrinogen concentration
clot firmness in cervid and bovid blood versus other mammals
candidate_data: Veterinary haematology reference intervals for cervids, bovids and leporids (e.g. Species360 ZIMS reference values).

label: The crocodile is the only animal that moves its upper jaw
claim: Animals in general move the lower jaw; the river crocodile is the only animal that moves the upper jaw.
quote: Animals in general move the lower jaw; the river crocodile is the only animal that moves the upper one.
measurable_quantities: mobility of upper jaw relative to skull (cranial kinesis) across taxa
candidate_data: Comparative cranial-kinesis literature on crocodilians, birds and snakes; MorphoSource skull scans.

label: The dolphin has true bone, not fish-spine
claim: The dolphin's skeleton is made of bone, like that of viviparous quadrupeds, not of fish-spine.
quote: The dolphin has bones, and not fish-spine.
measurable_quantities: skeletal tissue type in cetaceans
candidate_data: Cetacean osteology and skeletal scans in MorphoSource; Uberon tissue annotations.

label: Only the stag has solid branching horns, shed annually unless castrated
claim: Of all animals only the stag has horns that are solid throughout and branched, and only the deer sheds its horns, annually, unless it has been castrated.
quote: In the case of the stag alone of all animals the horns are solid throughout, and ramify into branches (or antlers). And, whereas no other animal is known to shed its horns, the deer sheds its horns annually, unless it has been castrated
measurable_quantities: antler versus horn structure
annual antler casting
antler cycle in castrated males
candidate_data: Cervid antler-cycle and castration literature; Animal Diversity Web accounts of horned ungulates.

label: All toed animals have nails except the elephant
claim: All animals that have feet with toes have nails, except the elephant, whose toes are undivided and slightly jointed and which has no nails at all.
quote: all animals have nails that have toes, and toes that have feet, except the elephant; and the elephant has toes undivided and slightly articulated, but has no nails whatsoever
measurable_quantities: presence of nails or hoof-like nails on elephant feet
nails or claws across toed taxa
candidate_data: Elephant foot anatomy literature; Phenoscape integumentary appendage annotations.

label: Viviparous footed animals have hair, oviparous footed have scutes, fishes scales
claim: All viviparous animals with feet have hair; all oviparous animals with feet have horny plates; and fishes, and only fishes, have scales.
quote: All viviparous animals furnished with feet have hair; all oviparous animals furnished with feet have horn-like tessellates; fishes, and fishes only, have scales
measurable_quantities: integument type (hair, scutes, scales) by taxon and reproductive mode
candidate_data: Phenoscape integument annotations; reproductive mode from AmphiBIO and the Reptile Database; Open Tree of Life for coverage.

label: Grey hairs are mostly white from the start, so greying is not withering
claim: Hair greys from the tip back toward the root, but most grey hairs are white from the beginning, which shows that greying is not a withering or decrepitude of the hair.
quote: Hair turns grey from the point backwards to the roots. But, in the majority of cases, grey hairs are white from the beginning; and this is a proof that greyness of hair does not, as some believe to be the case, imply withering or decrepitude
measurable_quantities: pigmentation along the length of greying hair shafts
candidate_data: Dermatological studies of hair-shaft pigmentation and greying.

label: Boys, women and castrated men never go bald
claim: No boy, no woman and no castrated man ever becomes bald, and a man castrated before puberty never grows the later hair (pubic, axillary, beard).
quote: For no boy ever gets bald, no woman, and no castrated man. In fact, if a man be castrated before reaching puberty, the later growths of hair never come at all
measurable_quantities: incidence of baldness in prepubertal boys, women and castrated men
secondary hair growth after prepubertal castration
candidate_data: Clinical literature on androgenetic alopecia and on eunuchs (e.g. Hamilton's studies of castrated men).

label: The crane is the only bird that changes colour with age
claim: No bird changes colour by reason of age except the crane, whose wings are ash-coloured at first and turn black as it grows old.
quote: no creature is liable to change of colour by reason of age, excepting the crane. The wings of this bird are ash-coloured at first, but as it grows old the wings get black.
measurable_quantities: age-related plumage colour change across bird species
candidate_data: Age-specific plumage descriptions in ornithological handbooks and the Birds of the World accounts.

label: Drinking water can make rams beget black lambs
claim: In many places the drinking water is of such a quality that rams that drink it before mating beget black lambs.
quote: water in many places is of such peculiar quality that rams, if they have intercourse with the female after drinking it, beget black lambs
measurable_quantities: lamb coat colour in relation to sire's drinking water source
candidate_data: Sheep coat-colour inheritance literature; controlled breeding records.

label: Blood forms first in the heart before the body is differentiated
claim: In development, blood appears first in the heart, before the body as a whole is differentiated.
quote: Blood is developed first of all in the heart of animals before the body is differentiated as a whole.
measurable_quantities: timing and site of first blood formation relative to body patterning in embryos
candidate_data: Developmental staging data for chick and mouse embryos; embryological literature on haematopoiesis.

label: All internally and externally viviparous animals, including cetaceans, have breasts
claim: All animals that are viviparous both internally and externally, including all hairy animals and the cetaceans (dolphin, porpoise, whale), have breasts and milk; oviparous animals and those only externally viviparous have neither.
quote: All animals have breasts that are internally and externally viviparous, as for instance all animals that have hair, as man and the horse; and the cetaceans, as the dolphin, the porpoise, and the whale-for these animals have breasts and are supplied with milk.
scope: viviparous animals (mammals, including cetaceans); fishes and birds
measurable_quantities: presence of mammary glands and lactation by taxon
candidate_data: Phenoscape and Uberon mammary gland annotations; Animal Diversity Web.

label: Camel's milk is thinnest, then human, then ass; cow's milk is thickest
claim: Of milks, the camel's is the thinnest, human milk next, then the ass's, and cow's milk is the thickest.
quote: Now the camel's milk is the thinnest, and that of the human species next after it, and that of the ass next again, but cow's milk is the thickest.
measurable_quantities: milk solids, fat and casein content by species
candidate_data: Published comparative milk composition tables for mammals (e.g. the Oftedal milk composition data).

label: Fertile sperm sinks in water, infertile sperm dissolves
claim: Sperm capable of impregnating sinks in water, while infertile sperm dissolves away.
quote: Sperm capable of impregnating or of fructification sinks in water; sperm incapable Of producing that result dissolves away.
scope: animals with blood (all of which emit sperm)
measurable_quantities: behaviour of fertile versus infertile semen samples in water
candidate_data: none known

label: Bloodless animals fall into four genera
claim: With very few exceptions, the animals without blood fall into four kinds: molluscs (cephalopods), crustaceans, testaceans (shelled molluscs and the like) and insects.
quote: All other animals may, with very few exceptions, be comprehended within four genera: to wit, molluscs, crustaceans, testaceans, and insects.
candidate_data: Open Tree of Life for comparing the grouping with modern invertebrate phylogeny.

label: Molluscs have eight feet with two rows of suckers, save one octopus
claim: All molluscs (cephalopods) have eight feet, each with a double row of suckers, except one species of octopus.
quote: All molluscs are furnished with eight feet, and in all cases these feet are severally furnished with a double row of suckers, with the exception of one single species of poulpe or octopus.
scope: molluscs in Aristotle's sense (cephalopods: octopus, cuttlefish, squid); the heledone (Eledone)
measurable_quantities: arm number
number of sucker rows per arm by cephalopod species
candidate_data: SeaLifeBase cephalopod species accounts; cephalopod taxonomic literature.

label: The octopus copulates with a special arm
claim: The octopus uses its last arm for copulation, and that arm is sharp, whitish and forked at its tip.
quote: the last of his feelers he employs in the act of copulation; and this last one, by the way, is extremely sharp, is exceptional as being of a whitish colour, and at its extremity is bifurcate
measurable_quantities: presence and form of a hectocotylized arm in male octopuses
candidate_data: Cephalopod reproductive anatomy literature; SeaLifeBase species accounts.

label: All cephalopods discharge ink when frightened, the cuttlefish most
claim: All molluscs (cephalopods) discharge a black juice when frightened, and the cuttlefish discharges it most copiously.
quote: All molluscs, when frightened, discharge such a juice, but the discharge is most copious in the cuttle-fish.
measurable_quantities: presence and size of ink sac
ink release in response to threat
candidate_data: Cephalopod anatomy and behaviour literature; SeaLifeBase.

label: Crawfish and crabs have ten feet including the claws
claim: The crawfish has five feet on each side including the claws, and the crab likewise has ten feet in all including the claws.
quote: The crawfishes have five feet on either side, including the claws at the end; and in like manner the crabs have ten feet in all, including the claws.
measurable_quantities: number of walking legs including chelipeds
candidate_data: Decapod morphology in SeaLifeBase and the World Register of Marine Species.

label: Lobsters always have one claw larger than the other, in both sexes
claim: In the lobster both male and female have one claw larger than the other, and no lobster of either sex is ever found with both claws the same size.
quote: There is no apparent difference between the male and female, for they both have one claw, whichever it may be, larger than the other, and neither male nor female is ever found with both claws of the same size.
measurable_quantities: claw asymmetry in male and female lobsters
candidate_data: Studies of cheliped asymmetry (crusher and cutter claws) in Homarus.

label: Crabs mostly have the right claw larger
claim: Crabs for the most part have the right claw bigger and stronger than the left.
quote: for the most part they have the right claw bigger and stronger than the left.
measurable_quantities: proportion of right-handed versus left-handed claw asymmetry in crab populations
candidate_data: Published field surveys of cheliped handedness in brachyuran crabs.

label: Spiral-shelled testaceans all coil to the right
claim: All spiral-shelled testaceans have their shells on the right-hand side and move in the direction opposite to the spire.
quote: all stromboid testaceans have their shells on the right hand side, and move not in the direction of the spire, but the opposite way.
measurable_quantities: proportion of dextral versus sinistral coiling across gastropod species
candidate_data: Gastropod shell-chirality surveys; MolluscaBase and the World Register of Marine Species.

label: Murex and trumpet-shell bore through other shells with a proboscis
claim: The purple murex and the trumpet-shell have a firm proboscis with which they bore right through the shells of the shellfish they prey on.
quote: so is that proboscis proportionately stronger in these testaceans; for they bore right through the shells of other shell-fish on which they prey.
measurable_quantities: drilling predation by muricid gastropods on bivalves
candidate_data: Literature on drilling predation by Muricidae; SeaLifeBase diet records.

label: The hermit crab is intermediate between crustaceans and testaceans
claim: The hermit crab is by nature like the crawfish but lives inside a shell like a testacean, and so is intermediate between crustaceans and testaceans.
quote: In its nature it resembles the crawfish kind, and it is born simple of itself, but by its habit of introducing itself into a shell and living there it resembles the testaceans, and so appears to partake of the characters of both kinds.
candidate_data: Open Tree of Life for the placement of hermit crabs among decapods.

label: Sea-urchins always have five egg masses
claim: The sea-urchin always has the same number of so-called eggs, an odd number, namely five, lying beneath the stomach.
quote: Underneath the stomach, in another membrane, are the so-called eggs, identical in number in all cases, and that number is always an odd number, to wit five.
measurable_quantities: number of gonads in sea-urchin species
candidate_data: Echinoid anatomy literature; SeaLifeBase and the World Register of Marine Species.

label: The sea-urchin's mouth is below because its food lies below
claim: The sea-urchin has its mouth underneath and its excretory outlet on top because its food lies below, so the mouth is placed where it is best suited to reach the food.
quote: For the food on which the creature lives lies down below; consequently the mouth has a position well adapted for getting at the food, and the excretion is above, near to the back of the shell.
candidate_data: none known

label: The sea-anemone has no excretion and so resembles a plant
claim: The sea-anemone appears to produce no excretion at all, and in this respect resembles a plant.
quote: The sea-nettle appears to be devoid altogether of excretion, and in this respect it resembles a plant.
measurable_quantities: egestion of undigested material through the mouth in anemones
candidate_data: Cnidarian feeding physiology literature.

label: Insects cut in two continue to live
claim: All insects continue to live when cut in two, except those that are cold by nature or so small that they chill quickly.
quote: All insects when cut in two continue to live, excepting such as are naturally cold by nature, or such as from their minute size chill rapidly
measurable_quantities: survival time and movement of bisected insect and myriapod body parts
candidate_data: none known

label: No two-winged insect has a sting in the rear
claim: No insect with only two wings has a sting at the rear of its body.
quote: no insect with only two wings has a sting in the rear.
measurable_quantities: presence of an abdominal sting in Diptera
candidate_data: Insect morphology databases and Diptera taxonomic literature.

label: The cicada has no mouth and feeds only on dew
claim: The cicada, alone of all creatures, has no mouth but a long tongue-like organ, and with it feeds on dew alone, so that no excrement is ever found in its stomach.
quote: by the aid of this the creature feeds on dew, and on dew only, and in its stomach no excretion is ever found.
measurable_quantities: cicada diet (xylem sap versus dew)
presence of excreta in the gut
candidate_data: Entomological literature on cicada xylem feeding and honeydew/excreta production.

label: There are exactly five senses
claim: There are five senses, sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch, and no other special sense is known.
quote: The total number of the senses (for we have no experience of any special sense not here included), is five: sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
candidate_data: Comparative sensory biology literature on additional modalities (electroreception, magnetoreception).

label: The mole has complete but stunted eyes hidden under the skin
claim: The mole is blind and has no visible eyes, but under the thick skin of the head it has stunted eyes containing all the parts of ordinary eyes.
quote: the eyes are found inside in a stunted condition, furnished with all the parts found in ordinary eyes
measurable_quantities: eye size and structure under the skin in moles
candidate_data: Anatomical and histological studies of eyes in Talpa and other moles.

label: Fishes hear and smell despite having no visible organs for either
claim: Although fishes have no visible organs of hearing or smell, they undoubtedly hear and smell, as shown by their fleeing from loud noises.
quote: but for all this fishes undoubtedly hear and smell. For they are observed to run away from any loud noise, such as would be made by the rowing of a galley
measurable_quantities: behavioural responses of fish to sound and odour
presence of inner ear and olfactory organs
candidate_data: Fish auditory and olfactory physiology literature.

label: Animals without lungs have no voice
claim: No animal can produce voice except by the action of the pharynx, so animals without lungs have no voice.
quote: no animal can give utterance to voice except by the action of the pharynx, and consequently such animals as are devoid of lung have no voice
measurable_quantities: mechanism of sound production across taxa
candidate_data: Comparative bioacoustics literature on sound production in fishes, insects and tetrapods.

label: No insect breathes
claim: Insects have no voice and make sound by internal air rather than by expelling air, because no insect breathes.
quote: they can emit sound by internal air or wind, though not by the emission of air or wind; for no insects are capable of respiration.
measurable_quantities: gas exchange in insects
mechanisms of insect sound production
candidate_data: Insect respiratory physiology literature on the tracheal system.

label: Language is peculiar to man
claim: Viviparous quadrupeds utter various vocal sounds but cannot converse; language is peculiar to man.
quote: Viviparous quadrupeds utter vocal sounds of different kinds, but they have no power of converse. In fact, this power, or language, is peculiar to man.
measurable_quantities: combinatorial structure of vocal communication across mammals
candidate_data: Comparative animal communication literature.

label: Bird song is learned and varies by locality
claim: Some young birds removed from the nest sing a different note from their parents after hearing other birds, so bird song is not wholly innate but can be modified and improved, and it varies by locality.
quote: Of little birds, some sing a different note from the parent birds, if they have been removed from the nest and have heard other birds singing
measurable_quantities: song of cross-fostered or tutored birds versus parental song
geographic song dialects
candidate_data: Song-learning and dialect studies; recordings in the Macaulay Library and xeno-canto.

label: Horses, dogs, oxen and all viviparous quadrupeds dream
claim: Not only men but horses, dogs, oxen, sheep, goats and all viviparous quadrupeds appear to dream, dogs showing it by barking in their sleep.
quote: it would appear that not only do men dream, but horses also, and dogs, and oxen; aye, and sheep, and goats, and all viviparous quadrupeds; and dogs show their dreaming by barking in their sleep.
measurable_quantities: presence of REM sleep and sleep vocalizations across mammals
candidate_data: Comparative mammalian sleep databases (e.g. the Savage and West sleep compilation) and REM sleep literature.

label: Fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans sleep, but briefly
claim: Water animals such as fishes, molluscs (cephalopods) and crustaceans undoubtedly sleep, though their sleep is very short.
quote: These animals sleep without doubt, although their sleep is of very short duration.
scope: fishes, cephalopods, crustaceans (crawfish and the like)
measurable_quantities: behavioural sleep criteria and sleep duration in fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans
candidate_data: Behavioural sleep studies in zebrafish, octopus and crayfish.

label: Cetaceans sleep with the blow-hole above the water
claim: The dolphin, the whale and all animals with a blow-hole sleep with the blow-hole above the surface, breathing through it while gently moving their fins.
quote: The dolphin and the whale, and all such as are furnished with a blow-hole, sleep with the blow-hole over the surface of the water
measurable_quantities: posture and breathing during sleep in cetaceans
candidate_data: Cetacean sleep studies (logging behaviour, unihemispheric sleep).

label: Sessile animals and testaceans have no separate sexes
claim: Animals that live fixed in one place have no distinction of sex, nor does any testacean.
quote: In animals that live confined to one spot there is no duality of sex; nor is there such, in fact, in any testaceans.
scope: sessile animals; testaceans (shelled molluscs, sea-urchins and the like)
measurable_quantities: sexual system (gonochoric or hermaphroditic) in sessile and shelled invertebrates
candidate_data: Sexual-system compilations for molluscs and echinoderms; SeaLifeBase reproduction fields.

label: The eel is neither male nor female and engenders nothing
claim: The eel is neither male nor female and produces no offspring; no eel has ever been seen with an egg.
quote: For instance, the eel is neither male nor female, and can engender nothing.
measurable_quantities: gonadal sex in eels
presence of eggs in eels
candidate_data: Anguilla reproductive biology literature; FishBase species accounts.

label: The psetta, erythrinus and channe are always found with eggs
claim: Among fishes, the psetta, the erythrinus and the channe are always found bearing eggs, having what bears and engenders but nothing that impregnates.
quote: so is it, among fishes, with the psetta, the erythrinus, and the channe; for these fish are in all cases found furnished with eggs.
scope: psetta, erythrinus, channe (channe is plausibly the comber, Serranus cabrilla)
measurable_quantities: presence of ovarian and testicular tissue in individuals of these species
candidate_data: FishBase reproduction fields; literature on hermaphroditism in Serranus.

label: Males larger in viviparous footed animals, females larger in egg-layers
claim: As a general rule, in viviparous footed animals with blood the male is larger and longer-lived than the female (the mule excepted), whereas in oviparous and larva-producing animals such as fishes and insects the female is larger than the male.
quote: in red-blooded animals furnished with feet and not oviparous, the male is larger and longer-lived than the female (except with the mule, where the female is longer-lived and bigger than the male); whereas in oviparous and vermiparous creatures, as in fishes and in insects, the female is larger than the male
scope: viviparous quadrupeds (mammals) versus fishes, insects, snakes, spiders, geckos, frogs
measurable_quantities: sexual size dimorphism by taxon
sex difference in lifespan
candidate_data: Sex-specific body size and lifespan in AnAge, the Amniote Life-History Database, FishBase and AmphiBIO.
